approach: per-length DFA with shared free suffix chain and merged boundary chains
details: Read L and R. Compute ellL equal to bit length of L and ellR equal to bit length of R. Create node START and node END. Build a shared free chain: for each k from 1 to ellR minus 1 create node FREE[k] whose two outgoing edges of weights 0 and 1 both point to FREE[k minus 1] where FREE[0] denotes END itself; so FREE[k] accepts any k-bit suffix. For each bit length ell from ellL through ellR decide a target node T and add a START edge of weight 1 to T; multiple weight-1 START edges to distinct targets are fine because each integer has a unique bit length so paths cannot collide. Determining T: if ell equals 1 then T is END; else let m equal ell minus 1; if ellL is strictly less than ell and ell is strictly less than ellR then T equals FREE[m] (full free suffix accepts any m bits); if ell equals ellL and ellL is strictly less than ellR then build a lower-bound chain BL of length m: BL[m] equals END; for i from 0 to m minus 1 let bit be the i-th most significant bit of Lsuffix where Lsuffix equals L minus two raised to power m; if that bit is 0 then BL[i] has edge weight 0 going to BL[i plus 1] and edge weight 1 going to FREE[m minus i minus 1]; if that bit is 1 then BL[i] has only a single edge weight 1 going to BL[i plus 1] (no 0-edge so any smaller number is rejected); T equals BL[0]. If ell equals ellR and ellR is strictly greater than ellL build symmetric upper-bound chain BR with Rsuffix equal to R minus two raised to power m: when bit at position i of Rsuffix is 1 then BR[i] has edge 1 to BR[i plus 1] and edge 0 to FREE[m minus i minus 1]; when that bit is 0 then BR[i] has only a single edge weight 0 to BR[i plus 1]; T equals BR[0]. If ellL equals ellR equals ell: find first index d in range 0 to m minus 1 where Lsuffix and Rsuffix bits differ (Lsuffix bit will be 0 and Rsuffix bit will be 1 at d); for i from 0 to d minus 1 the bit is forced equal in both bounds so create node C[i] with a single edge of that bit value going to C[i plus 1]; at C[d] add edge weight 0 to a BL-tail node BLtail[d plus 1] which is built using the same BL recipe applied to the remaining Lsuffix bits from position d plus 1 onward, and edge weight 1 to a BR-tail node BRtail[d plus 1] built using same BR recipe for the Rsuffix remainder; if Lsuffix equals Rsuffix exactly then d takes value m and just emit a forced chain of length m from C[0] to END (no branching needed); T equals C[0] when m is positive or END when m equals 0. Allocate fresh integer ids 1 through n for all logical nodes actually created (START, END, FREE[k] only for k values that are referenced, BL[i] for i in 0 to m minus 1, BR[i] for i in 0 to m minus 1, and C[i] in the combined case) keeping a map from logical labels to ids. Output n on first line; then for each node id 1 through n print that node outdegree followed by pairs (destination id, weight). Verify total n stays under 100; expected n is roughly 2 plus shared free chain length (at most 19) plus boundary chain lengths (each at most 19) giving about 60 worst case for ellL strictly less than ellR; the combined case stays under 50.
rationale: Iteration 0 needs a complete correct construction; this layered per-bit-length DFA with shared free suffix chain delivers around 60 nodes worst case versus the 100-node cap, providing a strong baseline score with straightforward correctness argument.

approach: backward construction sharing BL and BR nodes with FREE chain
details: Keep overall scaffold (per bit-length DFA with shared FREE suffix chain) but rebuild BL and BR backward from END to merge nodes with the FREE chain whenever functionally identical. Concretely: precompute (or lazily build) FREE[k] for k from 0 to ellR minus 1 where FREE[0] equals END and FREE[k] has both edges 0 and 1 going to FREE[k minus 1]. To build BL of length m for suffix Lsuffix, initialize BL[m] equal to FREE[0]. Walk i from m minus 1 down to 0: let bit be the i-th MSB bit of Lsuffix; if bit equals 0 AND BL[i plus 1] equals FREE[m minus i minus 1] then set BL[i] equal to FREE[m minus i] reusing the FREE chain node (no allocation); else allocate a fresh node for BL[i]. When allocating a new BL[i]: if bit equals 0 add edges (BL[i plus 1], 0) and (FREE[m minus i minus 1], 1); if bit equals 1 add only edge (BL[i plus 1], 1). Once a fresh node is allocated, all later (smaller i) positions also need fresh nodes since BL[i plus 1] will no longer equal a FREE node. Mirror this for BR: walk i from m minus 1 down to 0; bit equals 1 AND BR[i plus 1] equals FREE[m minus i minus 1] means BR[i] equals FREE[m minus i] (reuse); else allocate; allocated bit equals 1 case gets edges (BR[i plus 1], 1) and (FREE[m minus i minus 1], 0); allocated bit equals 0 case gets only edge (BR[i plus 1], 0). Apply the same backward-with-reuse construction to the BL tail and BR tail inside the combined ellL equals ellR case starting from position d plus 1 to m minus 1; also check whether the combined branch node C[d] can collapse to FREE[m minus d] (it can when both BL tail at d plus 1 and BR tail at d plus 1 equal FREE[m minus d minus 1], implying both branches go to the same FREE node — though correctness still requires C[d] to have BOTH edges 0 and 1; if both targets are FREE[m minus d minus 1] then C[d] is exactly FREE[m minus d] and no fresh node is needed). For Lsuffix equal to 0 (L is an exact power of 2) BL collapses entirely so T equals FREE[m]; for Rsuffix equal to 2 raised to m minus 1 (R is one less than a power of 2) BR collapses entirely so T equals FREE[m]. Build the FREE chain lazily — only allocate FREE[k] for k values actually referenced by START edges or boundary nodes. Keep START edges of weight 1 to each per-length target T(ell) unchanged. The combined case forced prefix C[0..d minus 1] remains a chain of fresh nodes since forced-bit-only nodes have no FREE equivalent.
rationale: This is a direct refinement of the iteration 0 layered DFA — still maturing — that exploits state equivalence between boundary chain nodes and the FREE chain (a node with both edges to FREE[k] is by definition FREE[k plus 1]) yielding up to m fewer BL or BR nodes when Lsuffix has trailing zeros or Rsuffix has trailing ones, plus full collapse when L or R is a power-of-two boundary.

approach: canonical state memoization keyed by level and accepted value interval
details: Replace the per-chain backward construction with a single recursive memoized builder getState(k, lo, hi) that returns the unique node accepting exactly the k-bit binary strings whose value lies in the closed interval lo to hi inclusive. Keep newNode helper and adj vector. Steps: read L and R; compute ellL and ellR as bit lengths; create START and END nodes (END is node id used directly for the k equals 0 base case when lo equals 0 and hi equals 0). Maintain unordered_map or std map with key tuple (k, lo, hi) mapping to int node id, where the special tuple (0, 0, 0) is pre-populated with END. Define getState(k, lo, hi): if lo is strictly greater than hi return sentinel value minus 1 (no node, caller will skip emitting that edge); if k equals 0 then lo must equal hi must equal 0 and return END; look up (k, lo, hi) in map and return cached node if present; allocate fresh node id, cache it BEFORE recursing to avoid infinite loops (the DAG is acyclic by level so this is safe but caching first is good practice); let half equal one shifted left by (k minus 1); compute lo0 equal to max(0, lo) and hi0 equal to min(half minus 1, hi); if lo0 is less than or equal to hi0 call child0 equals getState(k minus 1, lo0, hi0) and push edge (child0, 0) onto current node; compute lo1 equal to max(0, lo minus half) and hi1 equal to min(half minus 1, hi minus half); if lo1 is less than or equal to hi1 call child1 equals getState(k minus 1, lo1, hi1) and push edge (child1, 1); return current node. For START emission: loop ell from ellL to ellR; if ell equals 1 push edge (END, 1) onto START; else let m equal ell minus 1, compute losuf and hisuf for this ell as follows: if ell is strictly greater than ellL and ell is strictly less than ellR then losuf equals 0 and hisuf equals (one shifted left m) minus 1; if ell equals ellL and ell equals ellR then losuf equals L minus (one shifted left m) and hisuf equals R minus (one shifted left m); if ell equals ellL and ell is strictly less than ellR then losuf equals L minus (one shifted left m) and hisuf equals (one shifted left m) minus 1; if ell is strictly greater than ellL and ell equals ellR then losuf equals 0 and hisuf equals R minus (one shifted left m); call T equal getState(m, losuf, hisuf) and push edge (T, 1) onto START. Output as before: n on first line then for each node id 1 through n print outdegree followed by destination weight pairs. Why this can beat the current backward-sharing scheme: the FREE chain emerges naturally as getState(k, 0, (one shifted left k) minus 1) reused across all middle bit lengths; BL chain emerges as getState(k, Lsuffix mod (one shifted left k), (one shifted left k) minus 1) and automatically shares with FREE whenever the lo argument resolves to 0; BR chain emerges as getState(k, 0, Rsuffix mod (one shifted left k)) and shares with FREE whenever hi equals (one shifted left k) minus 1; the same length L equals R combined case becomes getState(m, Lsuffix, Rsuffix) and at every recursive level both halves may further collapse to FREE or to existing BL or BR nodes if their (k, lo, hi) tuples coincide. Crucially this catches cross structure merges the current code misses such as a combined tail node at level k equal to FREE k when both halves became unconstrained simultaneously even when the partial branch nodes never matched the FREE pattern, and merges where a BR tail at level k exactly equals a BL tail at level k for the same length problem after divergence (impossible when L is strictly less than R since intervals differ but possible when they coincide structurally for special inputs). Keep getState memoization map keyed by tuple of (int k, long long lo, long long hi) so identical recursive subproblems anywhere in the construction share a single node id.
rationale: Canonical (level, interval) memoization is the principled generalization of the current FREE chain reuse and is at least as compact as iteration 1 on every input while strictly more compact whenever any cross structure equivalence exists, continuing the maturing per length DFA direction toward the true minimum DFA size.

approach: prefix value multi length state DAG with profile memoization and parallel stop here edges
details: Reuse newNode and adj from iter 2 and add a map from string to int called profMemo. A suffix profile is a list of triples (m, lo, hi) with m at least 1, indicating accepted m bit suffix value intervals lo through hi inclusive. Serialize a profile by sorting triples by m ascending then concatenating m lo hi separated by hyphens. Procedure: read L and R; compute ellL and ellR as bit lengths; allocate START and END. Build state for prefix value 1 which is the unique depth one state after consuming the leading bit: profile P1 contains for each m from ellL minus 1 up to ellR minus 1 inclusive the triple (m, max(0, L minus (1 shifted left by m)), min((1 shifted left by m) minus 1, R minus (1 shifted left by m))) skipped when its lo exceeds its hi. Handle the empty suffix stop here case for integer 1: if L equals 1 add a START outgoing edge of weight 1 to END directly. If P1 is non empty add a START outgoing edge of weight 1 to buildNode(P1, prefixVal equal to 1). Function buildNode(profile, v): if profile is empty return negative one; serialize profile to key; if key already in profMemo return the cached node id; allocate fresh node id; cache the id under the key before recursing; for each bit b in 0 and 1 compute child_profile_b and a stopHere_b flag by iterating each triple (m, lo, hi) of profile: let half equal (1 shifted left by (m minus 1)); if b equals 0 set child_lo to max(0LL, lo) and child_hi to min(half minus 1, hi); if b equals 1 set child_lo to max(0LL, lo minus half) and child_hi to min(half minus 1, hi minus half); if child_lo exceeds child_hi skip this triple; if m equals 1 so the resulting child level is 0 representing the empty suffix and child_lo equals 0 and child_hi equals 0 set stopHere_b to true (this corresponds to 2 v plus b being inside [L, R]); else if m is at least 2 push triple (m minus 1, child_lo, child_hi) onto child_profile_b. After the sweep for bit b: if stopHere_b is true append an edge of weight b from current node to END; if child_profile_b is non empty call child_id equal buildNode(child_profile_b, 2 v plus b) and append an edge of weight b from current node to child_id. Return current node id. The current node can have up to four outgoing edges (one to END plus one to a continuation child for each of the two bit values) which exploits the problem allowance of multiple edges between the same pair of nodes carrying different weights or going to different destinations; each integer of bit length ell follows a unique path of length ell so two integers with different bit lengths exit via different parallel edges and never collide. Cross bit length sharing emerges automatically through profMemo: two prefix value states whose suffix interval signatures match at every relevant m share a single node; for example interior prefixes whose profile is the full interval at each m up to a common m_hi all collapse to the same FREE MULTI node giving a single shared chain for the interior; only boundary prefixes whose largest or smallest m carries a strict interval get fresh nodes when their signature differs from FREE MULTI. Output n then per node outdegree followed by destination weight pairs as before.
rationale: Canonical (k, lo, hi) per bit length memoization has matured at 90 across iter 1 and iter 2 with slope flat; lifting state characterization to general multi length suffix profiles with parallel stop here edges opens a new direction that exposes profile equivalences across different bit lengths and cases where boundary prefixes collapse into the FREE MULTI chain that the per length stratification cannot express.

approach: Brzozowski reverse subset construction yielding unambiguous NFA
details: Keep iter 3 forward profile construction intact and call it buildForward returning nForward and the forward adjacency. Add a reverse subset construction: precompute revAdj where revAdj[u][w] is the list of v such that forward has an edge from v to u of weight w. Subset construct D_R starting from the singleton subset containing only the forward END node: BFS over subsets keyed by sorted vector of forward node ids; for each subset S and each weight w in zero one compute T as the union of revAdj[u][w] for u in S; if T is non empty register T as a new subset id and record transition triple (S, w, T); cap subset count at nForward and bail back to the forward DFA if exceeded. A D_R subset is an accept iff it contains the forward START node. Build the output unambiguous NFA by reversing D_R: collapse ALL D_R accept subsets into one new merged start id; each non accept subset becomes its own NF node id; for each recorded D_R transition (S, w, T) emit NF edge from NF id of T to NF id of S of weight w; the NF end node is the NF id of the initial subset which is the singleton containing forward END. Set nReverse to NF node count. Pick whichever of forward DFA and reverse NFA uses fewer nodes; on tie keep forward. Renumber so the chosen graph has start at node id 1 and end somewhere within id range before printing. Merging multiple D_R accept subsets into one start is safe because D_R is deterministic so any string has at most one path through D_R and the reversed paths from the merged start therefore remain unique. NF nodes may have multiple parallel weight w outgoing edges to different targets which the problem allows; unique path per integer is preserved by the Brzozowski guarantee that D_R is a DFA. Implementation tips: hash subsets by encoding sorted vector of int ids into a string of decimal numbers separated by commas; use unordered_map from that string to subset int id; only nodes reachable in D_R from the initial subset are constructed so the practical D_R size is often much smaller than the worst case 2 to the nForward bound. Ensure the renumbering pass for NF emits node 1 as the merged start and that END is referenced consistently in adjacency lists.
rationale: Iter 3 profile memoization is the minimum DFA so the per length DFA direction has matured at 90 with flat slope across iter 1 to iter 3; Brzozowski reverse subset construction opens a fundamentally new direction by switching to unambiguous NFA which can have strictly fewer nodes than the minimum DFA whenever the LSB first state structure for [L R] is simpler than MSB first.

approach: Brzozowski reverse with merged accept tracking and relaxed bailout
details: Keep iter 4 forward profile DAG buildForward and revAdj construction unchanged. Replace the reverse subset BFS bailout logic. Old logic stopped construction the moment subsets.size() reached nForward; this is overly conservative because the final reverse NFA size equals numNonAcceptSubsets plus 1 after merging all accept subsets (those containing fwdStart) into a single merged start node. The actual reverse NFA can be much smaller than the raw subset count. New logic: during BFS, when a new subset is created, classify it immediately as accept or non-accept by checking whether fwdStart is in the sorted subset vector via binary_search. Maintain a running counter runningNonAcceptCount initialized to zero; when a non-accept subset is created increment it. Maintain a running flag anyAccept; when an accept subset is created set the flag. Compute currentReverseSize as runningNonAcceptCount plus (anyAccept then 1 else 0). Bailout only when currentReverseSize exceeds 99 (one less than the hard cap of 100) OR when subsets.size() exceeds say 4096 as a hard memory safety cap. Continue the BFS until natural termination otherwise. After BFS finishes without bailout, compute nReverse equals runningNonAcceptCount plus 1 (anyAccept must hold for a valid graph since the START needs reachability into FREE; if anyAccept is false fall back to forward). The final pick rule changes from (if nForward less or equal than nReverse use forward) to (if nForward less or equal than nReverse use forward else use reverse) which is the same logic but now nReverse is computed correctly even when subsets.size() exceeds nForward. Also fix one subtle thing: when subsetId.find finds an existing subset it must not double-increment the counters. Only newly created subsets update runningNonAcceptCount and anyAccept. Additionally consider: the initial subset (containing only fwdEnd) is currently created without being classified; classify it at creation time. Its acceptance status is whether fwdEnd equals fwdStart which is false (different nodes by construction); so initial subset is non-accept and increments runningNonAcceptCount. After all changes, nReverse may exceed nForward in some cases (fine, forward gets used) or be smaller (reverse used and yields a strictly smaller graph). Output through printGraph remains identical to iter 4 with the renumbering pass.
rationale: Iter 4 (Brzozowski) had only one attempt at score 90 so this direction is still maturing (Rule 1 maturity check); the explicit bailout fix targets the most likely reason iter 4 did not improve beyond forward: the conservative early-bailout often discarded reverse construction before its merged size could be measured against the actual cap.

approach: post construction disjoint length suffix state merging beyond minimum DFA
details: Keep iter 3 forward DFA buildNode and buildForward unchanged but during construction record each constructed node profile as a vector of triples (m, lo, hi) into a parallel global vector nodeProfile indexed by node id (push the input profile argument when the node is allocated and cached). After buildForward call a new function mergePass operating over non START non END internal nodes only. Substep A compute reachability bitsets reach[u] of size n bits for each node u by reverse topological order DFS: process children before parents and set reach[u] equal to bitwise OR over outgoing edges of u of (single bit for child c OR reach[c]); use vector of dynamic_bitset or vector of uint64 arrays since n is at most a few hundred. Substep B enumerate ordered candidate pairs (u, v) with u less than v among undeleted internal nodes; skip pair if reach[u] has bit v set or reach[v] has bit u set since one being reachable from the other forbids the merge by creating a cycle; check profile disjointness by sweeping nodeProfile[u] and nodeProfile[v] merged by m and confirming for every length m appearing in BOTH profiles the intervals satisfy u.hi(m) less than v.lo(m) or v.hi(m) less than u.lo(m); record disjoint non comparable pairs in a candidate list. Substep C greedy merge loop: repeatedly pick the disjoint candidate pair with smallest sum of outdegrees of u and v (favors low fanout merges first to keep merged outdegree under the 200 cap); allocate merged node id M (M may reuse u id and v marked deleted to avoid renumber churn); set adj[M] equal to deduplicated union of adj[u] and adj[v] where duplicates are exact (target, weight) matches; rewrite every predecessor edge whose target was u or v to point to M; set nodeProfile[M] equal to the disjoint length union of nodeProfile[u] and nodeProfile[v] taking interval union per m which is just the single interval since both contributed disjointly (concat triples sorted by m); mark v as deleted in a boolean array; recompute reach bitsets globally since the underlying DAG changed; regenerate candidate pair list considering only undeleted nodes and the new identity of M. Loop until candidate list becomes empty. Substep D compact node ids by walking 1 through n, skipping deleted, building a remap to 1 through n_merged where n_merged is undeleted count; rewrite all adjacency targets through remap; call printGraph with the compacted graph and remapped START and END. Compare n_merged against the original n_forward before merging and use whichever is smaller (the merge pass can only equal or shrink size so this guard is redundant safety). Why correctness holds: a merged node M whose constituent sub states u and v had disjoint length profiles preserves unique path per integer because each integer x of bit length ell traverses M at some specific path depth d; the remaining suffix length is ell minus d minus (depth from M to END); at M only one of u or v had ell minus d minus tail_length in its profile lengths so only that sub state outgoing edges lead to END for x; the other sub state outgoing edges from M lead into structures that cannot accept any string of x remaining suffix length and so contribute zero alternative paths; non comparability ensures the merge does not introduce cycles and the START node is untouched preserving its in degree zero; END is untouched preserving its out degree zero; multi edges between merged node and the same destination at different weights are explicitly allowed by the problem. Why savings appear: in the multi bit length case ellL is strictly less than ellR every BL chain node accepts strings of length in [1, ellL minus 1] while every BR chain node accepts strings of length in [1, ellR minus 1] and the intermediate FREE entries occupy lengths in [ellL, ellR minus 1]; many BL BR FREE pairs at different lengths become merge candidates collapsing the start fanout entries and the early chain layers into shared multi length nodes; in the same length case ellL equals ellR no length disjointness exists so the merge pass is a no op and the result matches iter 3 exactly.
rationale: Iter 4 and iter 5 Brzozowski reverse subset direction has produced two attempts both stuck at 90 so its slope is flat indicating that direction has matured; the iter 3 forward construction is the minimum DFA which cannot shrink further while staying a DFA but the problem only requires an unambiguous NFA where states with disjoint bit length profiles can collapse beyond DFA minimality; this opens a fundamentally new direction that exploits the interval language invariant that path length equals integer bit length and can break the 90 floor specifically on inputs with ellL strictly less than ellR.

approach: same depth disjoint length merging with edge dedupe safeguards
details: Revert to iter 3 forward profile DAG buildForward and add a strict same depth merge pass. After buildForward run BFS from START storing depth(u) for each node u with depth(START) equal to 0; the forward DAG is depth stratified meaning every edge goes from depth d to depth d plus 1 so same depth pairs have zero reachability and zero cycle risk. For each node u other than START and END compute mset(u) equal to set of m values appearing in any triple of nodeProfile[u]. Group nodes by depth; within each depth group enumerate candidate pairs (u, v) with u less than v and mset(u) intersect mset(v) empty. Greedy merge loop: pick the candidate pair within the lowest depth group whose merged outdegree is at most 200 where merged outdegree equals size of set union of adj[u] and adj[v] each entry being a (target id, weight) pair. Perform merge by setting adj[u] to sorted unique union of adj[u] and adj[v]; appending nodeProfile[v] triples to nodeProfile[u]; rewriting every predecessor p of v (p ranges over all undeleted nodes) replacing each edge whose first equals v plus 1 with first equals u plus 1 and then per source dedupe by reinserting adj[p] from a set of (target id, weight) pairs which preserves multi edges of different weights but removes exact duplicates; marking deleted[v] true and clearing adj[v]. Do not re run BFS depths since collapsing two same depth nodes preserves all other depths; re derive mset(u) for the merged node as union of pre merge msets which is the union of two disjoint sets by construction. Repeat until no candidate pair remains. Compact ids walking 1 through n in order skipping deleted ones and remapping all adjacency targets. Implementation safeguards: never include START or END in candidate pairs; defensively skip any pair where either node has zero recorded depth; after each merge re derive the candidate list rather than caching stale state; defensively skip any post merge edge whose target equals u plus 1 (a self loop) which cannot occur in a depth stratified DAG but is cheap to guard against. Output n on the first line then per node print outdegree followed by destination weight pairs. The iter 6 crash root cause was global reachability maintenance after each merge plus predecessor rewrite logic touching cross depth pairs which can induce cycles or stale reach bitsets; restricting merges to same depth pairs removes the need for reachability bitsets entirely and keeps predecessor rewrite local and idempotent; this is the same theoretical gain as iter 6 (disjoint length state merging beyond DFA minimality) but with a simpler safer implementation.
rationale: Iter 6 disjoint length merging is the only known way to break beyond DFA minimality which iter 1 through iter 5 all hit at 90 but iter 6 crashed; restricting merges to same depth pairs eliminates the cycle risk and predecessor rewrite bugs that caused that crash while preserving the full theoretical merging benefit so this continues maturing the post construction merging direction with a safer implementation.

approach: cross depth value interval merging with toposort verified atomic merge
details: Keep iter 3 buildNode and main flow including nodeProfile bookkeeping intact; replace the iter 7 same depth merge loop with cross depth merging that iterates all pairs regardless of depth. For each candidate pair (u, v) with u less than v, both non deleted, neither equal to START or END: first run valueIntervalDisjoint by sweeping nodeProfile[u] and nodeProfile[v] grouped by m and for every m appearing in BOTH profiles require max(lo_u, lo_v) strictly greater than min(hi_u, hi_v); pass if every shared m has disjoint intervals or no shared m exists; otherwise skip. Second run a merged outdegree check by building a set of (target id, weight) pairs across adj[u] and adj[v] and requiring size at most 200; otherwise skip. Third perform an atomic tentative merge with rollback: snapshot adj[u-1], adj[v-1], nodeProfile[u-1], the deleted vector, and adj[p-1] for every non deleted node p whose adjacency contained an edge to v; then mutate by setting adj[u-1] to the sorted unique union of adj[u-1] and adj[v-1] (entries are (target id, weight) pairs), appending nodeProfile[v-1] entries onto nodeProfile[u-1], iterating every non deleted node p and rewriting any edge whose target equals v to target u then deduping adj[p-1] via a set of (target id, weight) pairs, marking deleted[v] true and clearing adj[v-1]. Fourth verify acyclicity via a fresh Kahn topological sort over the tentative graph: compute the in degree of every non deleted node by sweeping every non deleted predecessor adjacency, push every zero in degree non deleted node onto a queue, pop a node and decrement in degrees of its successors enqueueing any successor whose in degree drops to zero, continue until the queue empties; if the total popped count equals the number of non deleted nodes the graph is acyclic and the merge commits (snapshot discarded); otherwise rollback by restoring every snapshotted vector verbatim and undeleting v. After a full pass over all pairs commits no merge, halt. Compact ids walking 1 through n in original order skipping deleted nodes, build a remap from old id to new id in range 1 through new_n, rewrite every adjacency target through the remap, and output new_n on the first line followed by per node outdegree and destination weight pairs. Implementation notes for safety: snapshotting only the touched predecessor adjacencies keeps rollback O(degree) per attempt; the dedupe via std set of std pair preserves multi edges to different targets at the same weight value while collapsing exact duplicates; the Kahn check uses only the live (non deleted) node subset so phantom edges from previously deleted nodes do not pollute it; rolling back v's deletion flag is critical so a later attempt can retry pairs involving v from a different angle.
rationale: Iter 6 cross depth merging with precomputed reachability bitsets crashed likely from stale bitset bookkeeping during the predecessor rewrite and iter 7 same depth restriction found no merges since profile memoization already canonicalizes same depth nodes; this iteration revives the cross depth direction using a fresh Kahn topological sort per merge attempt with atomic snapshot rollback that sidesteps stale state class bugs and additionally strengthens the disjointness check from m-set only to per m value interval which can catch merges between same depth same m nodes whose value ranges happen not to overlap, continuing to mature the post construction merging direction toward breaking the 90 plateau.

approach: cross depth language disjoint merging with pre merge reach bitsets and idempotent recompute
details: Branch from the clean profile DFA baseline 7d4bd0b; keep newNode and buildNode and buildForward identical including nodeProfile bookkeeping. Append a post construction merge pass with the following structure. Maintain a deleted boolean vector sized n plus one initially all false. Define recomputeReach as a function returning a vector of vector of uint64 sized n plus one by ceil of (n plus one) divided by 64 capturing for each non deleted node u the bitset of nodes reachable FROM u via outgoing edges over non deleted nodes (do NOT include u itself in its own bitset; only proper descendants). Compute it by running a fresh Kahn topological sort over non deleted nodes producing topo order then iterating topo from last to first: for each u in reverse topo order initialize reach[u] to all zero words then iterate each outgoing edge (c, w) in adj[u-1] where deleted[c] is false; set bit c in reach[u] by ORing word c shifted right by 6 with the mask one shifted left by (c AND 63) then OR every word of reach[c] into reach[u] word by word. Bit access uses word index id shifted right by 6 and bit position id AND 63. Define isMergeable(u, v) returning true iff both non deleted, neither equals START_NODE nor END_NODE, valueIntervalDisjoint(u, v) per length m (use the iter 8 helper unchanged: sweep nodeProfile[u-1] and nodeProfile[v-1] grouped by m and for every shared m verify max of los strictly greater than min of his), merged outdegree (size of a set of pair of int int holding adj[u-1] union adj[v-1]) is at most 200, AND bit v of reach[u] is zero AND bit u of reach[v] is zero. Main outer loop sets progress to false at start, calls recomputeReach once, then scans all pairs (u, v) with u strictly less than v in increasing u then increasing v order; the first pair for which isMergeable returns true performs the merge then sets progress to true and breaks back to the outer loop top where recomputeReach is called again. Merge procedure: build a std set of pair int int from adj[u-1] then insert each entry of adj[v-1] and reassign adj[u-1] to the set contents; append every triple of nodeProfile[v-1] onto nodeProfile[u-1]; iterate every non deleted predecessor p from 1 to n setting a touched flag false then for each entry in adj[p-1] if its first equals v set its first to u and touched to true; if touched then dedupe adj[p-1] by building a set of pair int int from it and reassigning; finally set deleted[v] to true and clear adj[v-1]. The outer loop terminates when a full pair scan produces no merge. Then compact ids by walking 1 to n skipping deleted entries and constructing a remap from old id to new id in range 1 to newN; rewrite all adjacency entries via the remap into a new adjacency vector sized newN; output newN on the first line then per node outdegree followed by destination id weight pairs. Why this differs from iter 8: iter 8 used post merge Kahn topological sort verify with snapshot rollback; this iteration uses pre merge reach bitset check which guarantees no cycle before mutation so no rollback path exists eliminating an entire class of state restoration bugs. Why this differs from iter 7: iter 7 restricted merges to same depth pairs and found none because profile memoization already canonicalizes same depth equivalents; cross depth pairs with disjoint length profiles (e.g. a BL node accepting length 4 strings in some interval and a FREE node accepting length 7 strings) are exactly the kind of pair the DFA minimization cannot collapse but the unambiguous NFA can. Correctness argument: the pre merge precondition reach[u] bit v equals zero AND reach[v] bit u equals zero means neither node reaches the other in the current DAG; after merging v into u the new u descendant set equals old Desc(u) union old Desc(v); the only possible cycle would require u to be in its own new descendant set which requires u in old Desc(u) (false because DAG) or u in old Desc(v) (false by precondition) so the post merge graph stays a DAG. Path uniqueness preserved: each integer x has a unique path before merge visiting either u or v or neither (never both since their profiles are length disjoint); after merge that path goes through the new u and the outgoing edges from new u carry both u and v children so for x with original suffix matching one of u or v exactly one child continues the unique path. Implementation notes: bitset size word count is ceil of (n plus one) divided by 64 which for n at most a few hundred is at most a handful of words; total recomputeReach cost is O(n squared) per call; total merge passes bounded by O(n) merges so overall O(n cubed) which for n at most 200 is at most about 8 million operations and runs in milliseconds; std set of pair int int handles edge dedup cleanly preserving distinct weight parallel edges between the same node pair. Defensive guard: skip any pair where adj[u-1] or adj[v-1] contains a self loop or a deleted target (should not occur but cheap to verify).
rationale: Iter 6 crashed on reach bitset bookkeeping and iter 8 crashed on post merge rollback complexity while iter 7 same depth restriction found no merges; this iteration combines iter 8 acyclicity safety with iter 6 reach bitset speed while sidestepping both crash classes by pre checking reach before mutation so the rollback path is eliminated entirely and continues maturing the only known direction able to break the 90 floor.

approach: prefix and suffix profile disjoint merging for unambiguous NFA compression
details: Start from the same depth merging baseline. Keep the existing prefix value multi length state DAG construction and Brzozowski style minimum DFA as the starting graph. The new step adds a second profile tracked per node: the prefix profile. For each node u maintain prefixProfile[u] as a list of (d, lo, hi) tuples meaning some path from START of binary length d with numeric value in [lo, hi] reaches u. Compute it by forward propagation: START has prefixProfile [(0, 0, 0)]. Walk nodes in topological order; for each edge u to c with weight b, push each tuple (d, lo, hi) of prefixProfile[u] into prefixProfile[c] as (d+1, 2*lo+b, 2*hi+b). After accumulation, normalize prefixProfile[c] by grouping tuples by d and taking the union of value intervals at that d; if at a given d the union covers everything reachable, keep that as one interval; else keep the merged sorted list of disjoint intervals. Reuse the same disjointness predicate from valueIntervalDisjoint but parameterize it over a profile argument so it works on suffix profiles (as before) and prefix profiles (new). Define isMergeable(u, v) as: u and v are not START or END; suffix profiles of u and v are length-wise disjoint (same predicate as before); prefix profiles of u and v are length-wise disjoint (new); merging does not violate outdegree cap of 200 after edge dedupe; no cycle is created (reach bitset check both directions). When merging u and v, replace both with a single node whose suffix profile and prefix profile are the union; rewrite all in-edges and out-edges. After one merge invalidate cached reach bitsets and recompute. Drive the loop: build DFA; compute prefix profiles via toposort propagation; recompute reach; greedy nested loop trying every pair (u, v); break inner loop on each successful merge to refresh state; outer loop terminates when a full pass found no merges. Edge cases: when a tuple lo equals hi treat it as a singleton; after pushing across an edge clamp lo and hi to non-negative; if the same prefix length appears in both u and v even with single overlapping value the merge must be rejected because it would create two distinct paths from START to the merged node accepting the same prefix.
rationale: Combining prefix language disjointness with suffix language disjointness is the formal unambiguity criterion for merging two DFA states into a single NFA node so this should push past the minimum DFA ceiling of 90 without introducing ambiguous paths.

approach: cross depth merging with path count verification for unambiguity
details: Branch from clean profile DFA baseline 7d4bd0b. Keep newNode, buildNode, profMemo, buildForward (the recursive interval profile construction) and nodeProfile bookkeeping intact. Add a post construction merge pass with strict path count verification. Step A define computeReach producing for each non deleted node u a bitset of proper descendants of u via Kahn topological sort over non deleted nodes processed in reverse topo order ORing word per word the bitset of each non deleted out edge child plus a bit set for the child id; bitset word count is ceil of (n plus 1) over 64. Step B define totalPathCount returning the number of distinct paths from START to END computed as follows: derive an upper bound for path length called maxLen as the bit length of R; allocate cnt as a two dimensional vector of long long sized (n plus 1) by (maxLen plus 2) all zero; set cnt at END at 0 to 1; iterate nodes in reverse topo order (Kahn over non deleted nodes); for each node u sum cnt at child at (k minus 1) for each out edge child c of u where deleted is false and k ranges 1 through maxLen plus 1; sum cnt at START across all k for the return value. The minimum DFA built by buildNode has exactly R minus L plus 1 paths from START to END since it accepts exactly the integers in [L, R] with a unique path each. Step C main merge loop: maintain deleted boolean vector and initialize all false; outer loop sets progress to false and recomputes reach; iterate pairs (u, v) with u strictly less than v skipping deleted, START, END; for each candidate check valueIntervalDisjoint on nodeProfile entries (per length m the value intervals must satisfy max of los strictly greater than min of his when m is shared); check bit v not set in reach at u and bit u not set in reach at v (no cycle would arise); check merged outdegree via a set of pair int int built from adj at u and adj at v is at most 200; if all pass perform a tentative merge with rollback: snapshot adj at u, adj at v, the deleted vector, and adj at p for every non deleted predecessor p that contains an edge whose first equals v; mutate by assigning adj at u to the set union sorted unique; append nodeProfile at v entries onto nodeProfile at u; rewrite every non deleted predecessor p replacing every edge with first equals v by an edge with first equals u then dedupe adj at p via a set of pair int int while excluding any self loop where target equals p; mark deleted at v true and clear adj at v; call totalPathCount; if result equals R minus L plus 1 the merge commits and the outer loop sets progress to true and breaks back to its top; else rollback by restoring every snapshotted vector verbatim and continue scanning. Step D after the outer loop produces no merge in a full pass compact ids by walking 1 through n in order skipping deleted entries; build remap from old id to new id in range 1 through newN; rewrite all adjacency targets via remap into a new adjacency vector sized newN; output newN on the first line then per node outdegree followed by destination weight pairs. Implementation tips: totalPathCount is O(n times maxLen) which for n at most a few hundred and maxLen at most 20 is a few thousand operations per call so cheap enough to invoke after every tentative merge attempt; cap totalPathCount return at 2 raised to 30 by clamping any cnt update that exceeds that bound to prevent overflow when an ambiguous merge multiplies path counts wildly; rollback always restores even when the merge succeeds is wrong so only restore on path count mismatch; the snapshot of predecessor adj must capture all p whose adj contains v before mutation since after mutation the original adj at p is lost; defensive guard skip any pair where adj at u or adj at v already contains a self loop or a target equal to a deleted node which should not occur but is cheap to verify. Correctness argument: the initial profile DFA has exactly R minus L plus 1 paths from START to END by construction unambiguity; any merge that preserves this exact count cannot have introduced an ambiguous path (which would add at least one to the count) nor dropped an accepted integer (which would subtract at least one); the cycle precondition ensures the merge yields a DAG; the outdegree cap is enforced; combined these guarantee the output is a valid DAG with unique paths per integer in [L, R] and no extra integers accepted. Why this beats previous attempts: iter 6 used reach bitsets without verifying outcome; iter 8 used post merge Kahn for acyclicity but did not verify unambiguity; iter 9 added pre merge reach for cycles but did not verify unambiguity; iter 10 added prefix and suffix profile disjointness as a static unambiguity proxy but the implementation likely had bookkeeping bugs; this iteration replaces the fragile static disjointness analysis with a single direct dynamic check that the language accepted by the merged graph still has cardinality R minus L plus 1 which is the strongest possible local check and admits any merge that is safe.
rationale: Iter 6 8 9 10 all crashed trying cross depth merging with various static disjointness analyses; replacing the static analyses with a single direct path count verification with rollback is a fundamentally simpler and stronger safety mechanism that should let actually safe merges commit while reliably rejecting unsafe ones thus breaking the 90 floor without crashing.

approach: hybrid forward and Brzozowski reverse bases each refined with path count verified merging
details: Extend the current iter 11 code which builds the forward profile DFA via buildNode and applies cross depth merging with path count verification. Refactor into two phases. Phase A build forward as today which produces n_f, adj_f, START_f, END_f, nodeProfile_f and the existing path count verified merge pass produces forward_merged_n and forward_merged_adj after compaction. Phase B start from the snapshot of the original pre merge forward DFA (re run buildNode into a separate adj_orig and nodeProfile_orig to avoid recomputing reverse from the merged graph which would be unsound). Build reverseAdj: for every edge u to v of weight w in adj_orig append the pair (u, w) into reverseAdj[v]. Run Brzozowski reverse subset construction: queue starts with the singleton subset containing END_f represented as a sorted vector of ints; maintain unordered_map keyed by the comma joined decimal serialization of the sorted vector mapping to a new subset id; for each popped subset S and each weight w in 0 and 1 compute T as the sorted unique union over u in S of reverseAdj[u][w]; if T is non empty look up or assign a subset id for T and record the triple (S id, w, T id); bailout to phase A result if subset count exceeds 200. A subset is accept iff it contains START_f via std binary search on the sorted vector. Reverse the recorded transitions: introduce NF nodes one per non accept subset plus exactly one merged_start node consolidating all accept subsets; for each recorded triple (S id, w, T id) emit an NF edge of weight w from NF id of T id to NF id of S id where accept subsets collapse to merged_start; NF start is merged_start; NF end is the NF id of the initial subset (the singleton containing END_f); renumber so START is id 1; populate a fresh nodeProfile by forward propagation in NF order computing reachable suffix interval per NF node (recursive buildSuffix that walks NF outgoing edges and for each edge (c, w) appends the triple (m plus 1, 2 lo plus w, 2 hi plus w) of every triple (m, lo, hi) of c profile and includes the base triple (1, w, w) when c equals NF end, then memoizes per node id and normalizes via union per m). Apply the SAME path count verified merge pass on this NF graph reusing computeReach valueIntervalDisjoint and totalPathCount unchanged producing reverse_merged_n. Phase C emit the graph (forward or reverse) whose merged n is smaller; tie favors forward; renumber so START is id 1 in output. Implementation notes: snapshotting between phases requires the global n adj START_NODE END_NODE nodeProfile deleted and profMemo to be reset between buildForward and buildReverse so use local vectors instead and pass them into helpers as parameters or wrap each phase in a fresh function scope with its own globals via a struct holding n adj START END nodeProfile deleted. Make computeReach valueIntervalDisjoint and totalPathCount operate on a graph parameter rather than globals. Important guard: if forward_merged_n is already at most 20 skip phase B since further savings unlikely and Brzozowski subset blowup risk; if Brzozowski subset count exceeds 200 use phase A result; if L equals R short circuit before both phases to a simple bit length plus 1 node chain.
rationale: Iter 4 to 5 Brzozowski standalone stuck at 90 and iter 11 forward DFA plus path count merging stuck at 90; both directions have matured individually but the combination has not been attempted; the reverse NFA has a fundamentally different LSB first state grouping than the forward MSB first DFA so the cross depth pairs that DO pass path count verification may exist in one base but not the other making the union strictly better.

approach: Kameda Weiner state pair grid with greedy prime cover for sub minimum DFA NFA
details: Branch from dd6f2fd. Replace the iter 12 forward plus reverse hybrid with a Kameda Weiner style minimum NFA construction. Phase A build forward profile DFA D_f via buildNode and profMemo as in iter 3 producing n_f states adj_f a START_f a END_f and a per state forward suffix profile pf_suffix (kept as the existing nodeProfile). Phase B build reverse DFA D_r via Brzozowski subset construction on D_f starting from the singleton subset containing END_f using revAdj where revAdj[u][w] is the list of v such that D_f has an edge from v to u of weight w; BFS subsets keyed by the comma joined decimal serialization of the sorted vector of D_f state ids producing n_r states adj_r with START_r being the subset containing END_f and accept subsets being those that contain START_f; merge all accept subsets into one END_r so D_r has exactly one accept state. Bail to iter 12 result if n_r exceeds 256. Phase C compute reachable strings per D_f state by forward BFS from START_f tracking pf_prefix per state as a vector of (d, lo, hi) triples meaning some path from START_f of binary length d with value in [lo, hi] reaches this D_f state; START_f starts with [(0, 0, 0)] and edges propagate via (d, lo, hi) becoming (d plus 1, 2 lo plus w, 2 hi plus w); normalize by grouping per d and taking interval union. Similarly compute reachable reverse prefixes per D_r state as pr_prefix tuples (d, lo, hi) representing length d reverse strings that reach that D_r state from START_r. Phase D build the relation grid M of size n_f by n_r where M[s_f][s_r] equals one iff there exists some accepted string of [L, R] that traverses s_f in D_f and traverses s_r in D_r; concretely M[s_f][s_r] equals one iff there exists a length d such that pf_prefix at s_f contains a triple (d, a, b) and pf_suffix at s_f contains a triple (m, lo, hi) with d plus m equals some bit length ell in [ellL, ellR] and the integer interval at (d, m) intersected with [L, R] is consistent with both s_f and s_r being on the same path; for simplicity use a direct construction: for each D_r state s_r compute its forward language as the set of pairs (d_total, [lo_total, hi_total]) representing accepted strings reaching END from s_r reversed; then M[s_f][s_r] equals one iff intersecting pf_suffix at s_f with the reversed forward language of s_r yields a non empty integer set. Phase E find maximal rectangles in M called primes by iterating over candidate row subsets I and column subsets J; a rectangle (I, J) is good iff M[i][j] equals one for every i in I and j in J; it is a prime iff adding any single row or column outside breaks the all ones property; enumerate primes greedily by sweeping rows and computing the maximal column subset where all selected rows have one. Phase F greedy prime cover: maintain a set of uncovered cells initialized to all (i, j) with M[i][j] equals one; repeatedly pick the prime covering the most uncovered cells and add it to the chosen set; mark its cells covered; halt when all are covered. Phase G build the resulting unambiguous NFA: for each chosen prime P_k create an NFA state n_k; for D_f START_f create NFA START which is the prime containing (START_f, START_r); for D_r END_r create NFA END which is the prime containing (any s_f with pf_suffix empty, END_r); transitions between primes derived by following D_f and D_r edges: there is an edge from prime P_a to prime P_b of weight w iff for every cell (s_f, s_r) in P_a there exists a cell (s_f prime, s_r prime) in P_b such that D_f has edge s_f to s_f prime of weight w and D_r has edge s_r prime to s_r of weight w (note D_r edge direction is reversed for our convention). Phase H verify the constructed NFA is acyclic via Kahn topological sort and verify total path count from NFA START to NFA END equals R minus L plus 1 by the totalPathCount helper applied to the NFA; if either check fails fall back to the iter 12 hybrid result. Phase I pick the smaller of the Kameda Weiner NFA size and the iter 12 hybrid forward and reverse merged sizes; output that graph with the standard renumbering so the chosen graph START is node id 1. Implementation guards: cap the number of primes considered at 256 to bound enumeration cost; cap pr_prefix and pf_prefix triple lists at 32 entries by merging adjacent intervals at the same d; if any phase exceeds time budget of 400 ms fall back to iter 12 result; the Brzozowski subset BFS uses unordered map keyed by comma joined decimal string of sorted ids as before; the prime enumeration uses bitsets of n_r bits per row to compute pairwise intersection of valid column sets fast.
rationale: Iter 11 and iter 12 path count merging both hit 90 because no candidate pair passes static disjointness plus path count check meaning the minimum DFA is at its true minimum for forward and reverse; Kameda Weiner state pair grid is the canonical construction for finding a smaller unambiguous NFA than the minimum DFA and exploits cross direction state correspondences that neither single direction can capture and is the next natural direction after both forward and reverse merging have flattened.

approach: constraint driven simultaneous multi node merging via union find with path count verification
details: Branch from dd6f2fd which already contains buildForward buildReverseDFA computeNFProfiles totalPathCount and the pairwise path count merge pass. Keep all of that intact for the easy single pair wins. After the existing mergePass converges on a graph add a new aggressive pass called batchMergePass that operates on the resulting graph. Step A enumerate seed pairs (u, v) with u strictly less than v skipping deleted START and END skipping pairs whose value interval profiles overlap at any shared bit length skipping pairs where one node reaches the other via the precomputed reach bitset. Step B for each seed pair run constraint propagation via a union find sized n plus one: initialize each non deleted node in its own class then union u and v; maintain a queue of class pairs to inspect starting with (find(u), find(v)); pop a class pair (A, B); for every node a in class A and every node b in class B and every weight w in 0 and 1 if a has an outgoing edge to c_a of weight w and b has an outgoing edge to c_b of weight w and find(c_a) is not find(c_b) then union c_a and c_b and push (find(c_a), find(c_b)) onto the queue; also if a has weight w edge to c_a and b has NO weight w edge then that is fine (no constraint); continue until queue empties. Step C after propagation reaches fixed point collect the set of non singleton classes; verify each class does not contain START or END (if it does abandon this seed); for each class verify it does not contain two nodes where one reaches the other via reach bitset (would create cycle); verify the merged outdegree of each class (size of set of pair int int over union of adj entries of class members) is at most 200. Step D tentatively perform all class merges atomically: snapshot adj of every node entire deleted vector and entire nodeProfile vector; for each non singleton class pick the smallest id as representative r; for every other member m in the class union the adj entries into adj at r via std set of pair int int dedupe append nodeProfile entries of m onto nodeProfile at r mark deleted at m true clear adj at m; then iterate every non deleted node p and for each edge in adj at p replace its first by find of first via the representative map then dedupe adj at p via a set of pair int int while excluding self loops where the destination equals p. Step E call totalPathCount and check the result equals R minus L plus 1; if so commit (discard snapshots); if not rollback by restoring every snapshotted vector verbatim. Step F restart enumeration from scratch since the graph has changed; halt when a full pass over seed pairs produces no commit. Step G run the batch merge pass on BOTH the forward DFA and the reverse NFA (after their respective single pair mergePass calls) then pick whichever resulting graph has fewer alive nodes as the final output following the existing iter 12 hybrid selection logic. Implementation notes for safety: the constraint propagation must not propagate when one of the involved nodes is deleted; the representative map for find must be rebuilt after each commit since node ids shift in terms of which is representative; cap the propagation queue length at say 4096 entries and abandon the seed if it overflows; if two classes need to be joined during propagation (their members already classified) just merge those two classes via union find and re queue the joined class against itself; the snapshot of nodeProfile must be a deep copy of the full vector since merged entries are appended; the reach bitset must be recomputed after each commit to reflect the new graph topology; defensive guard skip any seed where the union find finds itself trying to merge a class that includes START or END at any point during propagation by tracking a flag tainted on the union find that is set when START or END is ever unioned into a non singleton class.
rationale: Both single pair path count merging (iter 11) and Brzozowski hybrid (iter 12) hit 90 because individual pair merges introduce cross paths that the path count check rejects; the genuine NFA reduction below minimum DFA requires coordinated multi node merges where forced child merges cancel the cross paths introduced by parent merges; union find propagation makes that coordination automatic and the path count check at the end remains the strongest possible correctness verifier so this continues maturing the post construction merging direction while opening a fundamentally richer merge structure than any prior iteration.
